title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Concurrent Guaranteed Loans and Guaranty Issuance per Loan Number
content:
**1. Concurrent loans.** Under the VA Home Loan Guaranty a veteran may have more than one VA-guaranteed loan outstanding at the same time. There is no fixed limit on the number of such loans, as long as enough entitlement remains to support each new guaranty. A veteran may, for example, keep a former home with a VA loan as a rental while buying a new home with remaining entitlement.

**2. Separate records.** Each loan is its own record, with its own guaranty and its own entitlement charge.

**3. One guaranty per VA loan number.** A guaranty is issued only once for a given VA loan number. The test is made against VA's own loan records before a guaranty issues: where a loan record already carries that VA loan number, whatever that loan's present status (active, in default, paid in full, foreclosed or released by assumption), no second guaranty is issued for the number.

## The two rules side by side

| Situation (hypothetical) | Result |
|---|---|
| A veteran holds one guaranteed loan and closes a new loan under a different VA loan number, with enough remaining entitlement for its guaranty | The new loan receives its own guaranty and its own entitlement charge; the two loans stand side by side |
| A guaranty is sought under a VA loan number that already appears on a loan record now shown as paid in full | No guaranty is issued; the number has already received its guaranty |
| A veteran already holds three outstanding guaranteed loans | The count alone sets no limit; what matters is whether enough entitlement remains for the new guaranty |

## Points of judgement

- The number of loans is never the test; remaining entitlement is.
- The VA loan number is the object the once-only rule attaches to, and the loan records are the authority for whether it has already been used.
